issues.likelyCause: Under-extraction — usually grind too coarse, water not hot enough, or drawdown finished too fast.
issues.fix: Grind finer, and check your water is close to 96°C/205°F. Aim for a total drawdown time in the 2:30–3:30 range.

issues.likelyCause: Over-extraction — grind too fine, water too hot, or drawdown taking too long.
issues.fix: Grind slightly coarser. If drawdown is well past 3:30, that's your main signal.

issues.likelyCause: Channeling — pouring too fast, too close to the filter wall, or an unlevel bed.
issues.fix: Pour in slow, steady spirals starting from the center, and keep pours away from the very edge of the filter.

issues.likelyCause: Not enough coffee relative to water, or steep time too short.
issues.fix: Check your ratio against the recipe (French press ~1:16, AeroPress ~1:15) and don't cut the steep time short.

issues.symptom: Gritty or sludgy in the cup
issues.likelyCause: Grind too fine for the mesh filter, or plunged/pressed too aggressively.
issues.fix: Grind coarser for French press specifically — a mesh filter can't catch fine particles the way paper can. Press or plunge slowly.

issues.likelyCause: Over-steeped, or coffee left sitting on the grounds after brewing.
issues.fix: Pour out all the coffee immediately after plunging/pressing — don't let it continue steeping in the brewer.

issues.symptom: Shot is sour or watery, runs too fast
issues.likelyCause: Grind too coarse, or dose too low for the basket.
issues.fix: Grind finer in small increments and re-test — espresso is very sensitive to grind size. Confirm your dose matches the basket size.

issues.symptom: Shot is bitter, burnt, or runs too slow
issues.likelyCause: Grind too fine, or tamped unevenly causing excess resistance in spots.
issues.fix: Grind slightly coarser. Check your tamp is level — an uneven tamp causes channeling even in espresso.

issues.likelyCause: Stale beans (crema fades fast after roasting) or water not reaching full pressure/temperature.
issues.fix: Use beans within a few weeks of roast date, and confirm your machine is fully heated before pulling.

issues.likelyCause: Left on heat too long after brewing finished, or heat was too high.
issues.fix: Use medium-low heat and remove from heat the moment you hear the sputtering hiss at the end.

issues.likelyCause: Grind too coarse, or basket underfilled.
issues.fix: Grind a bit finer (finer than drip, coarser than espresso) and fill the basket level without packing it down.

issues.symptom: Little or no coffee comes through
issues.likelyCause: Grind too fine and choking flow, or the pot not sealed tightly.
issues.fix: Check the rubber gasket is seated properly and the pot is screwed on firmly; grind slightly coarser if it's still not flowing.

issues.symptom: Concentrate tastes weak even before diluting
issues.likelyCause: Ratio too diluted for a concentrate, or steep time too short.
issues.fix: Cold brew needs a much lower ratio than hot methods — aim close to 1:7. Don't steep less than 12 hours.

issues.likelyCause: Grind too coarse for the steep time, limiting extraction even over many hours.
issues.fix: Grind slightly finer — cold extraction is much slower than hot, so cold brew tolerates and often benefits from a finer grind than French press.

issues.symptom: Gritty sediment in the final drink
issues.likelyCause: Single-pass straining only through a mesh strainer.
issues.fix: Strain twice — mesh strainer first to remove the bulk of grounds, then a paper filter for the fine sediment.
